title: Beef Wellington
subtitle: Beef fillet wrapped in mushroom duxelles and puff pastry
excerpt: A beef fillet coated in mushroom duxelles and Parma ham, wrapped in puff pastry and baked until golden. The showstopper of British cooking, sliced at the table to reveal the pink centre.

recipe.sourceNotes: Beef Wellington is the most celebrated British celebration dish. Despite the name, its origins are unclear: it may have been named after the Duke of Wellington, or the name may simply have been applied to an existing preparation of beef in pastry (boeuf en croûte) that was fashionable in 19th-century Britain. The critical technique is the duxelles: mushrooms cooked down to a completely dry paste that contains no moisture. Wet duxelles will make the pastry soggy. Wrapping the beef in ham before the pastry provides a moisture barrier and adds flavour. The beef must be at room temperature before it goes in the oven, and it must be rested for 10 minutes before cutting to ensure an even pink interior.

recipeTools.notes: A large heavy pan for searing.
A baking tray lined with baking paper.

content.text: The duxelles must be completely dry before the Wellington is assembled: any remaining moisture will steam the pastry from the inside and make it soggy. Cook the mushrooms until all liquid has evaporated and the mixture looks almost paste-like. Chill everything before assembly. The pastry Wellington can be assembled and refrigerated up to 24 hours before baking, which suits a dinner party well.

items.preparation: thinly sliced; Parma ham is the traditional choice

content.text: Season the fillet generously with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a heavy pan until very hot. Sear the beef for 2 minutes on each side until deeply browned all over. Remove and brush immediately and generously with Dijon mustard. Chill for 30 minutes.

Fry the shallots and garlic in the same pan until soft. Add the mushrooms and thyme. Cook over high heat, stirring constantly, for 15 to 20 minutes until the mushrooms are completely dry and the mixture has darkened significantly. Season. Spread on a tray and chill.

Lay a large sheet of cling film on a work surface. Overlap the Parma ham slices in a rectangle large enough to wrap the fillet. Spread the cold duxelles evenly over the ham. Place the beef at the near edge and roll tightly, using the cling film to form a neat cylinder. Twist the ends and chill for 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 220 C / fan 200 C / gas 7. Unroll the pastry. Remove the cling film from the beef roll and place at one edge of the pastry. Roll tightly and seal the edges with egg wash. Place seam-side down on a lined baking tray. Brush all over with egg wash. Score lightly with a knife. Chill for 15 minutes.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is deep golden. A meat thermometer in the centre should read 52 C for rare-medium. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting into thick slices at the table.
